notes: Local corrections of the generated land where the frozen 2023 USGS raster predates what was built (tools/lib/terrain-overrides.mjs). World metres: +X east, +Z south.

A site's scope is its OSM areas plus traced polygons (add_xz), minus corridors round protected ways (exclude_ways) and traced polygons (exclude_xz), inside the land. The correction fades to exactly zero over edge_blend_m at the scope's edge, so the land outside the scope and on the coastline keeps its generated surface.

The site's grade is a harmonic membrane on a grid_m grid (relaxation over-relaxation factor, a fixed number of iterations): it takes the generated land outside the scope and the level and profile targets inside their shapes, and is as smooth as possible everywhere else, so the 32 m land grid's waves smooth out and designed surfaces meet their surroundings in gentle ramps. Regions apply in order: level holds a flat elevation_m inside its shape, profile holds control elevations_m along its line, sink cuts depth_m below the grade with a smoothstep rim side_run_m wide. Shapes: points_xz (optionally grown by buffer_m, negative to inset), line_xz with width_m, or an ellipse (center_xz, radii_m, rotation_deg turning +X toward +Z).

Every 32 m land cell the correction reaches is re-meshed as a quadtree of leaves down to min_leaf_m, split until each leaf's two triangles stay within tolerance_m of the corrected surface (sampled every sample_m); shared edges stay watertight, coarse neighbours keep their surface.
All elevations, depths and rims here are production inference for game art, traced from the designer's plan and dated photos, not survey data.

sites.name: Cityside Park
sites.evidence: OSM w1428380753 (leisure=park, 2025-09-09); CMG/TIDA Phase 1 site plan 2025-04-16 (event lawn, stormwater treatment areas, forebay, promenade); SFAC art-location plan 2024-02 (Stormwater Bioretention Area x3, Stormwater Channel); Esri World Imagery 2026-05-26 and 2025-08-29; CMG photos (Sep 2025 to Oct 2026), Google Maps contributor photos ph05, ph08, ph10 (Sep 2025). The 2023 USGS raster (CA_SanFrancisco_B23) predates the 2024-2025 grading: it shows a pit where the lawn is and fill mounds along the future promenade.

exclude_ways.reason: Avenue of the Palms: its carriageway, parking lanes, curbs, sidewalks and the street ground beside them (planting strips, verges, the west palms) keep their generated surface; the cycle track runs inside this corridor.

exclude_xz.reason: The fenced lawn lot south-east of the park (Jun 2026 pano p10, aerial 2026-05-26): the OSM park polygon takes in its north-west corner up to the construction-panel fence, which is not part of the opened park.

The two land cells beside Isle House (w1249412094) stay as generated: re-meshing them would split the cells under the building and re-cut the foundation its landmark form matches. Only the park's edge strip by the avenue lies here, where the grade follows the USGS land anyway.

regions.reason: The light concrete promenade and the dark path inside it run level along the riprap crest (aerial 2026-05-26, CMG photos); north of the lawn the 2023 raster already shows the old shore path at 3.0-3.1 m. The line is the OSM Perimeter Path (w1530613461) moved 1.4 m seaward to the photographed band's middle; the south end rises gently to the Waterfront Plaza.

The oval event lawn and its asphalt ring path read flat in every photo (cmg04, cmg12, cmg13, ph05); level with the promenade beside it. The 2023 raster has a pit there (2.0-2.9 m), filled when the park was built.
The north stormwater bioretention beds between the lawn ring and the cycle track (SFAC plan: Stormwater Bioretention Area; S9: basins and channels): a shallow planted basin below the paths.
The central stormwater meadow (ph08 Sep 2025): a shallow planted basin round the decomposed-granite meander.
The bioretention round the pump station (CMG site plan 2025-04-16: stormwater gardens, conveyance swale, forebay).
The conveyance swale from the south plaza to the forebay (the curved channel edge on the 2025-08-29 aerial).
The level concrete pad of the stormwater pump station (aerial 2025-08-29: a 16 by 11 m box parallel to the avenue; cmg04).
The oval stormwater forebay beside the pump station (CMG plan label, aerial 2025-08-29 and 2026-05-26: about 7.5 by 4.7 m).
